artifacts.title: Problem frame & constraints
artifacts.task: Define the user/business outcome, explicit non-goals, prohibited behavior, quality target, latency/availability target, cost envelope, data sensitivity, reversibility, and decisions that remain human-owned.
rubric: Measurable success criteria exist.
Hard constraints are separated from preferences.
Irreversible/high-consequence decisions have an owner.
Non-goals prevent architecture creep.

artifacts.title: Architecture decision record
artifacts.task: Choose workflow vs agentic vs augmented-LLM architecture, model tier, context strategy, and orchestration pattern. Record at least two rejected alternatives.
rubric: Decision is tied to stated constraints.
At least two plausible alternatives are rejected for explicit trade-offs.
Complexity is justified rather than assumed.
Revisit triggers are defined.

artifacts.title: Integration & trust-boundary map
artifacts.task: Map APIs, MCP servers, retrieval/data stores, credentials, authorization, tool capabilities, trust boundaries, and failure propagation.
rubric: Every external capability has an auth boundary.
Least privilege is explicit.
Failure paths are visible, not only happy paths.
Sensitive data movement is traceable.

artifacts.title: Evaluation & release gates
artifacts.task: Define representative evaluation data, metrics, deterministic checks, model/human graders where needed, slice-level regressions, and release-blocking thresholds.
rubric: Metrics correspond to user/business risk.
Critical slices cannot be hidden by aggregate scores.
Release gates are defined before the test result is known.
Regression runs are repeatable.

artifacts.title: Safety & governance matrix
artifacts.task: For each material risk, define preventive control, detective control, corrective action, owner, evidence artifact, and residual risk.
rubric: Controls are placed before irreversible actions when possible.
Human review follows a risk rule, not blanket review.
Each risk has an accountable owner.
Evidence can be audited later.

artifacts.title: Cost & latency budget
artifacts.task: Model call/token assumptions, cacheable prefixes, routing, batching, throughput, tail latency, and the thresholds that trigger architecture changes.
rubric: Budget assumptions are explicit.
Optimization preserves the evaluated quality/safety floor.
Tail latency is considered, not only averages.
Caching/routing choices have invalidation or fallback rules.

artifacts.title: Observability & operations
artifacts.task: Define traces, metrics, alerts, slow-drift reviews, incident ownership, and first diagnostic actions for retrieval, prompt, model, tool, and permission failures.
rubric: Signals map to specific failure layers.
First diagnostic action is stated for each major failure class.
Ownership and escalation are explicit.
Slow quality drift is covered in addition to outages.

artifacts.title: Stakeholder brief
artifacts.task: Explain the same architecture for executive/security/legal stakeholders in terms of value, trade-offs, residual risk, reversibility, ownership, and evidence.
rubric: Technical details are translated into business consequence.
Residual risks are not hidden.
Trade-offs are presented with alternatives.
Decision/approval owners are clear.

artifacts.title: Handoff package
artifacts.task: Create the runbook, architecture rationale, open assumptions, owner map, change criteria, known failure modes, and enough evidence that another architect can safely modify the system.
rubric: Another team can operate and change the system.
Assumptions and unknowns are explicit.
Decision rationale survives team handoff.
Change/revalidation triggers are documented.

stress_tests.title: Stale retrieval after refresh
stress_tests.task: A content refresh completes, but answers still cite old facts. State where you investigate first, what evidence confirms the failure layer, and the structural fix.

stress_tests.title: Over-privileged tool
stress_tests.task: A tool can mutate resources outside the task scope. Redesign the control boundary without relying on prompt instructions.

stress_tests.title: Hidden evaluation regression
stress_tests.task: Aggregate quality improves after a model/prompt change while one regulated user slice degrades. Decide the release outcome and diagnostic path.

stress_tests.title: Cost / latency drift
stress_tests.task: Tail latency and cost rise after context/caching behavior changes. Identify evidence needed before changing the model or architecture.

stress_tests.title: Irreversible stakeholder request
stress_tests.task: A stakeholder requests an action the agent can execute autonomously but that cannot be safely reversed. Place the approval/control boundary and justify it.
